name: Central bank stress
summary: Bank of England raises Bank Rate to 4% on 5 Nov and warns inflation will near 5%
state: The Bank of England raised Bank Rate from 3.75% to 4% on 5 Nov, its first rise since 2023, and warned inflation will approach 5% as the energy shock feeds through (CNBC; Bank of England). Australia's central bank hiked to 4.85% on 3 Nov, and the ECB and Bank of Japan held in late October. Policymakers face a stagflationary dilemma; no emergency move has been made.
for_you: Borrowing costs are rising again in several economies; variable-rate mortgages and new loans are most exposed.
rubric_hit: Stagflationary dilemma at major central banks = Watch; no emergency moves

sources.title: CNBC — Bank of England hikes interest rate for the first time since Iran war
Bank of England — Interest rates and Bank Rate

why: Central banks are the shock absorbers; when they are boxed in or their independence is challenged, markets lose their backstop.
drivers: Inflation vs growth trade-off, political pressure, currency moves, financial stability.

rubric.alert: Emergency inter-meeting moves, attempt to remove a central-bank head, or coordinated intervention.
rubric.watch: Stagflationary dilemma, open political pressure on a major central bank, or FX intervention by a G7 bank.
rubric.normal: Fed, ECB and BoJ acting orderly and on schedule; independence unquestioned.
